title: Mariner Workflows - model selection and runtime scouting call
summary: Initial scoping call to understand Mariner's requirements for a production LLM deployment across hosted vs dedicated vs private; heavy emphasis on multilingual support, long-context document processing, and tool-calling for internal search and orchestration. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs and security compliance requirements (SSO, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a short live benchmark and follow up with security docs and pricing options.
topics: deployment mode tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
next_steps: Redwood to share security/architecture pack (SOC2, KMS, VPC guide) by 2028-11-12
Run a 48-hour benchmark with sample docs (Redwood + Mariner) - Redwood to schedule
Follow-up technical deep-dive for infra team week of 2028-11-20
Send draft pricing for hosted vs dedicated pilot
action_items: Alex Green: share SOC2 and KMS integration docs - due 2028-11-12
Samira Patel: schedule benchmark run and invite Mariner data samples - due 2028-11-13
Marcus Holt: provide network constraints and existing VPC CIDR - due 2028-11-11
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-11-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), Jordan (ML Eng), Marcus (Infra), Lea (Product)

Summary (auto): initial discovery on models and deployment.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya (CTO): yeah loud and clear. thanks for doing this on short notice.
[00:10] Alex (AE): awesome. quick intros then we'll jump into your use cases. i'm alex, i lead the account for redwood. samira and diego are our solutions folks.
[00:20] Samira (SE): hi all, excited to dig into the long-doc use case you mentioned in the intake form.
[00:27] Jordan (ML Eng): yeah thanks. high level — we process large operational manuals, multi-lingual, often 30k to 120k tokens per customer. so context length is non-trivial.
[00:40] Priya (CTO): and we want tool-calling to run internal search, database lookups, and trigger workflows — not just plain text generation.
[00:50] Diego (SE): got it. that maps to tool-calling + retrieval augmented generation. do you currently use an external retriever?
[00:58] Marcus (Infra): we have an elasticsearch cluster and a couple of vector DBs for experiments, mostly we use Vectorix — um, it's called Vecstore internally.
[01:08] Lea (Product): and our success criteria are: sub-500ms median latency for interactive queries, cost under $0.015 per 1k tokens on production routes, and zero data leakage off-prem for regulated customers.
[01:22] Alex (AE): thanks. high-level we want to map those to redwood modes: hosted for fast onboarding, dedicated for predictable throughput and lower e2e cost, private for strict data residency/V P C constraints. we'll talk model choices that fit long context and multilingual.
[01:38] Priya (CTO): quick question — how do you handle K V cache with long context? we saw K V cache issues in other runtimes, memory blow-ups.
[01:46] Samira (SE): good callout. redwood's runtime does continuous kv caching with eviction tuned to sequence length distribution; we also expose quantization profiles that reduce memory per token. sometimes we recommend hybrid approach: chunking + a retrieval layer so models see only a focused window and the retriever provides the rest.
[02:05] Jordan (ML Eng): on models — open-models are preferred. we ran trials with mistral-mix and a few L L M variants but haven't settled. any guidance on multilingual vs performance tradeoffs?
[02:18] Diego (SE): yes there are tradeoffs: some open models (mistral, openflamingo variants) have strong English throughput but weaker low-resource languages. we can surface per-language quality and cost profiles from our model catalog. for 100k token pipelines we often recommend a combination: a long-context encoder (specialized variant) to do retrieval-aware summarization, then a smaller chat model for final compositional responses.
[02:41] Priya (CTO): can you do function calling / tool-calling in hosted? we need signed requests to internal APIs and a way to rotate keys with our KMS.
[02:52] Samira (SE): absolutely. hosted supports function/tool calling and we integrate with customer K M S for key rotation. for private deployments you get customer-managed K M S and full network controls (V P C peering, private endpoints).
[03:05] Marcus (Infra): security question — SOC 2? and can we get audit logs for every token? we need per-request metadata for compliance.
[03:13] Alex (AE): yes SOC 2, and we provide detailed audit logs and token-level traces in the console. for private we can ship logs into your SIEM or S3 behind your V P C.
[03:24] Lea (Product): on latency — you said sub-500ms. how does batching affect that when you have heavy traffic spikes?
[03:32] Samira (SE): we recommend workload-aware batching. Dedicated pools can be reserved to reduce variance; hosted has burst capacity but if you need strict p99 latency, dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or private with pinned nodes is the way to go.
[03:46] Jordan (ML Eng): curious about quantization — does redwood support 4-bit quant on A100 and also int8 on newer hardware? we've seen quality regressions.
[03:55] Diego (SE): yes both. we provide quantization profiles and run quality regression checks tied to your eval prompts. we can auto-suggest profiles per model and per workload. you can also pin a model version that uses a specific quant profile to avoid surprises.
[04:10] Priya (CTO): for our pilot we want to try a hosted proof-of-concept first with 10k-document subset, then move to dedicated if economics look good. is that a common path?
[04:19] Alex (AE): very common. hosted for fast feedback, then dedicated reserved pools for production. some customers go private for compliance at the start, but most iterate hosted -> dedicated -> private.
[04:28] Marcus (Infra): networking — we need to know egress IPs for allow-listing and support for V P C peering. also, we might be under FedRAMP later so region and data residency matter.
[04:38] Samira (SE): we'll include V P C peering docs and region options in the pack. for FedRAMP-level needs we have a private path and partners that can help.
[04:46] Jordan (ML Eng): about the retrieval integration — can we plug our Vecstore directly or do you require a particular vector DB?
[04:54] Diego (SE): we integrate with popular vector DBs and also provide a lightweight retriever if you want. for high throughput we recommend colocating vector DB with the runtime or using our dedicated colocated pools.
[05:05] Priya (CTO): pricing — can you ballpark hosted vs dedicated for our scale? we expect peak 50 qps with burst to 200 for 10-15 minute windows.
[05:14] Alex (AE): rough number — hosted per-token is higher but no infra management; dedicated amortizes to lower per-token cost with reserved monthly commit. we'll send tailored pricing after we see your sample workload.
[05:25] Lea (Product): do you have per-language benchmarks? we need Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese at minimum.
[05:31] Samira (SE): yes we'll share per-language BLEU/ROUGE-style evals and human evals we've run across models in our catalog.
[05:38] Jordan (ML Eng): one more — context >100k tokens. how do you recommend handling?
[05:44] Diego (SE): usually chunk + retrieval + progressive summarization works best: ingest big doc, build vector index, synthesize compressed context windows, use a long-context model for chunk-level synthesis then a shorter chat model for user-facing prompts. we also support models with extended kv windows — but they are expensive; often hybrid gives better cost/perf.
[06:05] Priya (CTO): are there any redwood-specific gotchas when moving to private? like feature differences?
[06:11] Samira (SE): functionally they're parity but private requires you to manage some infra pieces — K M S, network, monitoring retention. we also have a private control plane option where we handle orchestration but keep data paths private. we'll document the options.
[06:25] Alex (AE): ok let's talk pilot scope. suggestion: 2-week hosted pilot with 48-hour focused benchmark: ingest 10k docs, run retrieval+tool-calling flows, measure latency, cost, quality. you provide sample docs and test prompts.
[06:38] Priya (CTO): sounds good. questions about model selection — can you recommend 2-3 model variants for the pilot (one long-context, one multilingual, one cost-optimized)?
[06:47] Samira (SE): yes our proposal: 1) Long-context specialized variant (we'll propose an open long-context model tuned for chunking), 2) Multilingual large model (strong JP/ES/PT), 3) Cost-optimized quantized variant for high-throughput routes. we'll send per-model expected latency and token-cost estimates.
[07:02] Marcus (Infra): also we want to run a small end-to-end test that includes tool-calling to our internal job scheduler — need signed calls and role-based access.
[07:10] Diego (SE): we can run that in the benchmark; we support signed JWTs and on-call rotation via K M S.
[07:17] Lea (Product): ok that's useful. any blockers we should surface?
[07:20] Alex (AE): none obvious — we need your sample docs, network constraints, and a list of eval prompts. we'll send an onboarding checklist.
[07:29] Priya (CTO): timeline — we want results within two weeks; can you commit to that?
[07:33] Alex (AE): yes we'll prioritize. Samira will run the setup.
[07:36] Samira (SE): i'll own the bench, i'll reach out for S3 creds or an upload link.
[07:40] Jordan (ML Eng): note: our docs include PII fields for some customers; redwood handling of redaction or masking during bench?
[07:47] Diego (SE): we'll advise on masking and provide local-only runs if needed; for hosted tests we can do obfuscated data or run the benchmark on private deployment if you prefer.
[07:58] Priya (CTO): ok final — can you send us a short architecture note and suggested pilot plan after the call?
[08:03] Alex (AE): yes — action items and next steps we captured.
[08:07] Priya (CTO): perfect thanks everyone.

End transcript notes: occasional transcription errors around acronyms (V P C, K M S, K V cache) noted and normalized in the summary.

Attachments referenced: "pilot-onboarding-checklist.pdf" (shared), "per-language-benchmarks.xlsx" (will be shared), "security-architecture-pack.zip" (to be sent).
